name: Screens & teen mental health
brief: Is social media harming adolescents' mental health? Parents, platforms and governments want an answer.

stages.ask: How do teenagers themselves describe their social-media use and its effects?
How common are heavy use and depressive symptoms, and do they co-occur?
Does heavy use come before rising symptoms, or the other way round?
Does cutting use for four weeks improve mood?
What do all the trials and cohorts add up to?

name: Microplastics in our bodies
brief: Microplastics turn up in blood, placentas and arteries. Are they a health problem?

stages.ask: What has been studied so far, with which methods, and where are the gaps?
Do different labs measuring the same tissue sample find the same particle counts?
How much do people carry, and does it vary by region and age?
Do people with more microplastics in arterial plaque have more heart attacks later?
Through what cellular mechanism could particles cause inflammation, and at what dose?

name: A soft gripper for fruit picking
brief: Growers can't find seasonal workers. Can a soft robotic gripper pick strawberries without bruising them?

stages.ask: What gripper designs exist, and how have they been evaluated?
Design a gripper that growers and pickers find usable.
Which combination of finger material, pressure and approach speed minimizes bruising?
Does it beat existing grippers on a shared set of fruits and metrics?
Can it run a full shift in a real greenhouse? Will staff keep using it?

name: The four-day week
brief: A government wants to know if a 32-hour week at full pay is good for workers and firms.

stages.ask: How did the first companies that tried it make it work, or fail?
Can firms be recruited, and can productivity and well-being be measured consistently?
Sixty firms volunteered and all will switch eventually. Does it affect burnout and output?
A whole country adopted it by law in one year. What happened to national productivity?
Why does it work in some sectors and not in others?

name: A new post-viral syndrome
brief: Months after a new infection, some people report exhaustion and brain fog. What is it, and what helps?

stages.ask: What do the first patients look like?
How common is it among people who were infected?
Who is at risk? Does vaccination before infection change the odds?
Twelve candidate treatments are proposed. Which work?
Ranking the treatments when few were compared head-to-head.

name: AI triage in the emergency department
brief: A hospital group wants an AI tool that flags patients who will need intensive care.

stages.ask: Can routine data predict ICU admission within 24 hours?
Does it still work at another hospital, a year later?
Do nurses agree with each other, and with the tool, on the triage level?
The tool will be switched on in all 8 hospitals this year. Does it save lives?
Why do some clinicians override it so often?
